C0.quote: voters cast approval ballots, two finalists are selected, and a runoff election
C0.note: Distortion of approval voting with runoff rules.

C1.quote: the best distortion achievable by approval voting with (majority) runoff is Θ(𝑚 2 )
C1.note: Main results are distortion bounds. Section 7 has simulations on synthetic data and PrefLib-based utilities (utilities are generated synthetically).

C2.2.quote: each voter approves an unranked subset of the candidates
C2.2.note: First-stage input is approval sets; the runoff uses rankings consistent with utilities.

C2.3.quote: each voter 𝑖 ∈ 𝑁 has a utility function 𝑢𝑖 : 𝐶 → R⩾0

C2.4.quote: the vote that each voter submits stems from his utilities
C2.4.note: Utilities u_i are notated separately from approval votes π_i; ballots are induced from utilities by a threshold.

C3.1.note: No analysis considers voters misreporting; ballots are induced by a fixed threshold rule.

C3.2.quote: each voter only approves the candidates for which his utility is higher
C3.2.note: The paper states in words that ballots follow utilities (implicit utilitarian assumption).

C3.3.quote: we use the implicit utilitarian framework introduced by Procaccia and Rosenschein
C3.3.note: Justified by reference to the framework in prior work.

C4.1.quote: each voter approves all the candidates for which she has utility at least 𝜏

C4.2.note: The term dichotomous preferences is not used.

C5.1.quote: Define the distortion of a distribution over candidates
C5.1.note: Social welfare and distortion are the evaluation criteria.

C5.2.quote: dist(𝑥, 𝑢) ® = max𝑐 ∈𝐶 SW(𝑐, 𝑢) ® / SW(𝑥, 𝑢)
C5.2.note: Welfare is evaluated on the cardinal utilities, which are separate from the ballots.

VOT.quote_behav: each voter only approves the candidates for which his utility is higher
VOT.note: Voters mechanically approve by threshold and vote in the runoff by ranking.

ORG.note: The election designer picks the rules and the threshold as part of the analysis, which is treated as the designer (DES).

DES.quote_behav: we seek a pair-selection rule, which selects a pair of candidates
DES.quote_info: we do not have access to the utilities
DES.note: The designer's objective is explicit: minimize worst-case distortion. The designer sees only approval ballots and rankings, not the utilities.

C7.1.note: Voters are NONSTRAT; the designer is STRAT in an optimizing sense, but not in the same analysis as voters acting strategically. The designer is arguably not an agent taking an action, so I took it conservatively.

C8.1.note: The designer's choice is a worst-case optimization (minimax distortion), which is not a game-theoretic solution concept.

C9.2.note: The needed assumptions (ballots induced by a common-threshold utility, ranking consistent with utility, unit-sum utilities) are stated.
